terms.gloss: produce, the fruits of the land
evidence: Cic. Off. 2.12: frūgum frūctuumque reliquōrum perceptiō (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Everything a field, an orchard or a herd yields; in the singular, a crop, or the profit from something. Fruit to eat is pōma (see fruit).

terms.gloss: crops, the fruits of the earth (above all grain and pulses)
terms.comment: The dative frūgī is also the adjective “honest, thrifty” (see well-behaved).

phrases.latin: vēr enim tamquam adulēscentiam significat ostenditque frūctūs futūrōs, reliqua autem tempora dēmetendīs frūctibus et percipiendīs accommodāta sunt
phrases.english: for spring stands for youth, as it were, and shows the produce to come; the other seasons are suited to harvesting and gathering it in

phrases.latin: tū cursū, dea, mēnstruō mētiēns iter annuum, rūstica agricolae bonīs tēcta frūgibus explēs
phrases.english: you, goddess, measuring out the year’s journey in your monthly course, fill the farmer’s country house with good crops
